story-context.story-summary: Create an async HTTP client (IntentsClient) to communicate with agentic-memories Intents API. This client provides CRUD operations, polling for due intents, claiming intents for exclusive processing, and reporting execution results. Follows the established MemoryClient pattern with circuit breaker, error handling, and Langfuse observability.

criterion.title: CRUD Operations
Polling & Worker Operations
criterion.description: IntentsClient must support worker polling and execution: - get_pending(trigger_type, user_id) → GET /v1/intents/pending Returns due intents, excludes already-claimed intents Includes in_cooldown flag in metadata for condition triggers - claim_intent(id) → POST /v1/intents/{id}/claim Claims intent for exclusive processing (prevents race conditions) Returns IntentClaimResponse with intent and claimed_at Returns 409 Conflict if already claimed within 5 minutes Uses FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED for multi-worker safety - fire_intent(id, report) → POST /v1/intents/{id}/fire Reports execution result: success, failed, gate_blocked, condition_not_met Clears claimed_at (releases claim) Returns cooldown_active, cooldown_remaining_hours, last_condition_fire Updates execution_count and last_executed - get_history(id, limit, offset) → GET /v1/intents/{id}/history Returns execution audit trail ordered by executed_at DESC Includes timing metrics (evaluation_ms, generation_ms, delivery_ms)

criterion.title: Error Handling
criterion.description: Robust error handling with circuit breaker: - Raises IntentsClientError with context on failures - Logs errors with trigger/user details - Circuit breaker integration (reuse pattern from MemoryClient) - Network errors → IntentsNetworkError - API errors → IntentsAPIError

criterion.title: Observability
criterion.description: Langfuse tracing for all operations: - Operations traced as spans with @observe() decorator - Duration and success/failure logged - Include operation name, trigger_id, user_id in metadata

pattern.name: HTTP Client Pattern (MemoryClient)
pattern.description: Complete async HTTP client pattern using httpx.AsyncClient: - Class structure with __init__, __aenter__, __aexit__, close() - URL from config (AGENTIC_MEMORIES_URL) - Custom exception hierarchy (MemoryClientError, MemoryNetworkError, MemoryAPIError) - Error handling with detailed logging - Timeout configuration (DEFAULT_TIMEOUT) - health_check() method returning bool

key-code-snippets.snippet: Class initialization pattern: - Load URL from config with fallback - Initialize httpx.AsyncClient with timeout and headers - Structured logging with logger.info()

HTTP request error handling pattern: - try/except for httpx.TimeoutException, NetworkError, ConnectError, HTTPError - Duration tracking (start_time, duration_ms) - Detailed error logging with extra context - Custom exception raising with original_error
health_check() implementation: - GET request to /health endpoint - Returns bool (True if 200, False otherwise) - Exception handling with logger.warning

pattern.name: Circuit Breaker Pattern (MemoryManager)
pattern.description: Circuit breaker implementation for graceful degradation: - Failure counter (_circuit_breaker_failures) - Opened timestamp (_circuit_breaker_opened_at) - Configurable threshold (CIRCUIT_BREAKER_THRESHOLD = 5) - Configurable timeout (CIRCUIT_BREAKER_TIMEOUT = 900 seconds) - _is_circuit_breaker_open() check method - Reset on success

key-code-snippets.snippet: Circuit breaker constants: CIRCUIT_BREAKER_THRESHOLD = 5 # Failures before circuit opens CIRCUIT_BREAKER_TIMEOUT = 900 # 15 minutes
Check before operation: if self._is_circuit_breaker_open(): logger.warning("Circuit breaker is open, queueing...") return False
Reset on success: self._circuit_breaker_failures = 0 self._circuit_breaker_opened_at = None
Increment on failure: self._circuit_breaker_failures += 1 if self._circuit_breaker_failures >= self.CIRCUIT_BREAKER_THRESHOLD: self._circuit_breaker_opened_at = time.time()
_is_circuit_breaker_open() method: - Check if opened_at is set - Calculate elapsed time - Auto-close after timeout - Return bool

pattern.name: Langfuse Tracing Pattern
pattern.description: Langfuse integration using @observe() decorator and manual tracing: - Import langfuse.decorators.observe with LANGFUSE_AVAILABLE flag - No-op decorator if Langfuse not available - @observe(name="...", as_type="trace"|"span") on async methods - Automatic input/output/duration/error capture

key-code-snippets.snippet: Usage on async method: @observe(name="memory_storage", as_type="trace") async def store_conversation_memory(self, ...): # Automatic tracing of inputs, outputs, duration

pattern.name: Error Classes Pattern
pattern.description: Exception hierarchy for HTTP client errors: - Base class: ClientError(Exception) - Network errors: NetworkError(ClientError) - service unreachable - API errors: APIError(ClientError) - service returned error response - Custom __init__ to capture error context

pattern.name: Structured Logging Pattern
pattern.description: Consistent structured logging with extra context: - logger = get_logger(__name__) - logger.info/debug/warning/error with extra={} dict - Always include duration_ms for operations - Include user_id, conversation_id, request identifiers - Log inputs at DEBUG level, results at INFO level

api-schema.description: agentic-memories Intents API v1 schema (from Epic 6 in review)

endpoint.request-body: { "user_id": "string", "intent_name": "string", "description": "string", "trigger_type": "cron" | "interval" | "once" | "price" | "silence" | "portfolio", "trigger_schedule": { "cron": "string (optional)", "interval_minutes": "int (optional)", "trigger_at": "datetime (optional)", "check_interval_minutes": "int (optional)", "timezone": "string (optional, user's timezone)" }, "trigger_condition": { "expression": "string (e.g., 'NVDA < 130')", "condition_type": "price" | "portfolio" | "silence", "cooldown_hours": "int (minimum hours between fires)", "fire_mode": "once" | "recurring" }, "action_type": "notify" | "check_in" | "briefing" | "analysis" | "reminder", "action_context": "dict (rich LLM briefing)", "action_priority": "low" | "normal" | "high" | "urgent", "expires_at": "datetime (optional)", "max_executions": "int (optional)", "metadata": "dict (optional)" }

endpoint.description: Returns intents that are due for processing. Excludes already-claimed intents. For condition triggers, includes in_cooldown flag in metadata.
Claims an intent for exclusive processing. Uses FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED for multi-worker safety. Returns 409 Conflict if already claimed within 5 minutes.
endpoint.error-responses: 409 Conflict: Intent already claimed within 5 minutes

endpoint.description: Reports execution result. Clears claimed_at, updates execution counters. For condition triggers, updates last_condition_fire and returns cooldown info.
Returns execution audit trail ordered by executed_at DESC. Includes timing metrics.

file-to-create.description:
New file implementing IntentsClient class. Follow MemoryClient pattern exactly:
1. Import statements (httpx, time, Optional, Dict, Any, get_config, get_logger) 2. Exception classes (IntentsClientError, IntentsNetworkError, IntentsAPIError) 3. IntentsClient class: - DEFAULT_INTENTS_URL constant - DEFAULT_TIMEOUT constant (30 seconds recommended) - __init__(intents_url, timeout) - load from config - __aenter__, __aexit__, close() - async context manager - create_intent(data: dict) -> dict - list_intents(user_id: str, filters: dict = None) -> list - get_intent(id: str) -> dict - update_intent(id: str, data: dict) -> dict - delete_intent(id: str) -> bool - get_pending(trigger_type: str = None, user_id: str = None) -> list - claim_intent(id: str) -> dict (handle 409 specially) - fire_intent(id: str, report: dict) -> dict - get_history(id: str, limit: int = 50, offset: int = 0) -> list - health_check() -> bool
4. Error handling: - httpx.TimeoutException -> IntentsNetworkError - httpx.NetworkError, httpx.ConnectError -> IntentsNetworkError - httpx.HTTPError -> IntentsNetworkError - status_code != expected -> IntentsAPIError - Special case: 409 Conflict on claim_intent (expected, not error)
5. Logging: - DEBUG: before each operation - INFO: after successful operation - ERROR: on failures - Always include: duration_ms, intent_id/user_id when available
6. Langfuse: - @observe() decorator not needed for client methods (too granular) - Client will be called from traced contexts (MemoryManager, MCP tools) - Those callers will have @observe() and client calls appear as sub-spans

testing-approach.description:
Testing strategy for IntentsClient:
1. Unit tests (pytest-asyncio): - Mock httpx.AsyncClient responses - Test each CRUD operation - Test error handling paths - Test 409 Conflict handling on claim_intent
2. Integration tests: - Requires running agentic-memories service - Test full CRUD lifecycle - Test pending/claim/fire workflow - Verify circuit breaker behavior
3. Manual testing: - Use /health/full to verify connectivity - Create test intent via IntentsClient - List, update, delete test intent - Verify Langfuse traces appear

verification-checklist.item: All CRUD methods work against agentic-memories
Claim returns 409 Conflict when intent already claimed
Fire clears claim and updates counters
Circuit breaker activates after 5 consecutive failures
Langfuse traces appear for traced callers
Health check endpoint includes intents_api status
All exceptions include proper context (user_id, intent_id, error details)
Async context manager cleanup works (no leaked connections)

notes.note: This is the foundation for Epic 13. All other stories depend on this client. Follow MemoryClient pattern exactly to maintain consistency.
The claim_intent method must handle 409 Conflict as a normal flow, not an error. This happens when multiple workers try to claim the same intent - it's expected behavior.
Circuit breaker is critical for proactive worker reliability. If agentic-memories goes down, we don't want workers to constantly retry and waste resources.
agentic-memories Epic 6 is still in review. If API changes during implementation, update this client accordingly. The API is stable enough to start implementation.
Default timeout of 30 seconds is appropriate for intents operations (faster than memory storage which involves LLM extraction). Adjust if needed based on testing.
